scope: Authored calculation inputs; benchmark values are not measurements of pyramid stone
assumptions: Molar masses are rounded formula masses; carbonate mass agrees with NIST WebBook. No parameter is fitted to the social post.
Density is an illustrative constant for quartz, not measured granite density. Molar volume is computed as molar mass divided by density.
Fluxes are a sensitivity sweep, not inferred rates for any carbonate or hydroxide experiment.
The Arrhenius ratio holds other solution conditions and mechanism fixed within the cited aqueous study's 100–200 °C interval. It is not a molten-salt extrapolation.
Detection probabilities are hypothetical conditional probabilities. Multiplication uses the chain rule; repeated-context calculations additionally assume independent, equivalent contexts.
